text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has launched a fishermen's fund to help them obtain interest-free loans to finance fishing activities.
-- The government plans to introduce stiffer punishment for offenders of mobile phone-number frauds, said Deputy Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Chan Kong Hoy.
-- Acting PM Anwar said the government will be firm in its efforts to curb corruption and misuse of power among top leaders.

-- The introduction of ringgit futures trading on the New York Cotton Exchange will have minimal impact of spot ringgit dealings, said NYCE director of marketing and member services Tim Barry in New York.
-- The fight against corruption will not be confined to top Malaysian party UMNO but will cover other parties of the ruling National Front, said Acting PM Anwar.
